audit.whatIsWrong: Both layers treat the Q stun as if it could land at any time. The full layer says 'stuns at 3 passive stacks' once, in a line the player never sees, and the content layer just says 'his Q tongue stun lets him land a free trade'.
audit.why: An Acquired Taste builds a stack every time Tahm Kench damages you; Tongue Lash stuns only when it lands on a target already carrying three stacks, consuming them. That makes the stun the most telegraphed hard CC in the lane — it is countable, and a Nasus who counts it knows exactly which walk-up is safe and which is a free trade for Kench.
audit.corrected: Count his An Acquired Taste stacks; the stun is only live on the third proc. Tongue Lash is 7/6.5/6/5.5/5s.
sources: champ-data/_kits/tahmkench.json — P An Acquired Taste, Q Tongue Lash

audit.whatIsWrong: The content layer calls the grey-health shield his 'passive' in wants.foe[1], whys[1], early and mid.
audit.why: Thick Skin (E) is what stores a percentage of damage taken and converts it to a shield, and it is on a 3s cooldown. The passive is An Acquired Taste, which is the stun/Devour counter. Naming the wrong slot means the player baits the wrong thing.
audit.corrected: Thick Skin (E) is the grey-health shield; An Acquired Taste (P) is the stack counter.

audit.whatIsWrong: Nothing in either layer tells the player that chip damage is the wrong trading pattern here.
audit.why: Thick Skin stores a percentage of the damage he takes and gives it back as a shield on a 3s cooldown, plus an out-of-combat heal from the same stored pool. Poking Tahm Kench with Spirit Fire ticks and single autos literally funds his shield. Nasus is one of the few champions who can answer that, because a stacked Siphoning Strike is one large number instead of many small ones.
audit.corrected: Bank stacks and spend them in one burst window rather than chipping; the chip is refunded.
sources: champ-data/_kits/tahmkench.json — E Thick Skin description and cooldown

audit.whatIsWrong: The packet flags this matchup as having no cooldown-sequencing advice anywhere, and it was right — every line was "respect him" with no clock on it.
audit.why: Two numbers carry this lane: Tongue Lash at 7/6.5/6/5.5/5s and Abyssal Dive at 21/20/19/18/17s. Abyssal Dive is both his engage and his only escape, so once it is spent there is no second commitment and no way out.
audit.corrected: Explicit wait-then-act sequencing added at phases[2], phases[4], breakdown.cooldowns, dosFull[0] and content spikes[1].

audit.whatIsWrong: No Grievous Wounds anywhere in a matchup where three of his five abilities heal or shield.
audit.why: Tongue Lash heals him on champion hit, Thick Skin heals out of combat from stored damage, and Devour shields. Nasus grinds with Soul Eater lifesteal, so whoever holds the healing advantage wins the long fight.
audit.corrected: Flagged for the itemization block; I did not force it into an edit because the writable itemization string is inside report[], which I cannot address safely.

audit.whatIsWrong: The full-layer chart gives Tahm Kench stages 1-4; the content chart gives him only stages 1-2 and calls 3-5 Skill.
audit.why: Nasus wins 50.59% over 427 games, a genuinely even lane, and Wither is a hard answer to a champion whose whole kit needs him to walk into auto range.
audit.corrected: phases[2].side and phases[3].side should read Skill, and phases[6].side should read Skill rather than Nasus. I could not propose those edits: the token "Tahm Kench" is 10 characters and "Skill" is 5, so the ±10% length band rejects every side flip in this matchup. Reported instead.
